perOption.reason: Coffee appears in the sentence right before the blank, so this option exerts real pull. But the coffee was cited as a rationalization for avoiding work (an example of an unscheduled break), not as a claim about caffeine dependence. 'Instead' must contrast with taking unscheduled breaks; avoiding caffeine does not fill that contrast, and the passage never criticizes caffeine itself.

The passage's thesis: scheduled breaks (planned at appropriate times) keep you on track; unscheduled breaks are unwarranted and cause procrastination. 'So to prevent procrastination, vow to stick strictly to your planned intervals instead' — 'planned intervals' maps to the scheduled breaks, and 'instead' correctly contrasts with taking unscheduled breaks. Grammatical seam is a clean imperative; logic matches perfectly.
Working-hour length is never discussed. The passage is about when to take breaks within work hours, not about reducing total hours. No textual support; 'instead' contrast fails.

Polar-opposite trap: 'spontaneous moments of rest' is precisely an unscheduled break, which the passage condemns as a sure-fire route to procrastination. Attractive only to a reader who anchors on the opening clause 'breaks are necessary to revive your energy' and misses the scheduled-vs-unscheduled contrast.

Echoes 'revive your energy levels' from the first sentence, but the passage's prescription is structural adherence to a pre-made schedule, not continuous self-monitoring of energy. Constant evaluation would arguably invite more mid-work interruptions; the 'instead' contrast with unscheduled breaks does not hold.

note: Solved blind as a top-tier examinee.
